text: Weather page fix: when the backyard air sensor fails its quality check (it has been reading AQI 500 on and off, a sign it needs cleaning), the page now shows the EPA monitor’s reading and says why, instead of “unavailable,” and the 24-hour air chart leaves out the faulty hours
During a power shutoff, neighbors can now tap “my power’s back” or “still out” on the home and Fire pages; once most say it’s back, the site says so, often hours before SCE’s map does
When SCE is restoring our power, the site now says so plainly: power often comes back to some streets before SCE’s map catches up
Live power status: the top of every page now says when SCE has shut off our power (or is about to), with SCE’s estimate for when it’s back, straight from SCE’s outage map and rechecked every minute
Events has two new filters: ✨ New (anything added in the past week) and 🎁 Giveaways (free things for kids to take home)
A fire that’s 75% or more contained no longer sets off alerts (the Fire page headline, the status bar and the group-chat alert); it stays on the fire list and map with its containment

Events now include Valencia Town Center’s happenings (Mall-o-Ween trick-or-treating on Oct 31) and free kids’ giveaways at local stores, marked 🎁 Giveaway, starting with Geoffrey’s birthday at Toys"R"Us inside Macy’s, Oct 16–17
Tidied up: the Fire page is shorter (planned roadwork, the fire-history archive and the camera card are gone), and the 24/7 phone numbers now live in one tap-to-call list
The Halloween treat map is now one tap from the home page, through Halloween night
Power shutoffs: the alert on the Fire page now follows SCE’s shutoff list for our own circuit, so it says when SCE may cut our power and when it’s back on, and marks shutoffs nearby as not ours
New: a list of neighbor-owned businesses. Own a business and live in Tesoro Highlands? It’s free to be on it — fill in the form on the page, and it appears once it’s approved
A toy drive: a neighbor is collecting brand-new toys by Saturday, Oct 17, for a giveaway to families in need

New: a Halloween treat map for the houses behind the gate, with the Gardens Park party drawn in. Tap your house to add it as “knock or ring” or “candy out front,” then flip it to out of candy on the night. Neighbors only; the code is in the community WhatsApp group
The Halloween party moved to Friday, Oct 30 (6–10 PM, Gardens Park) — now with pizza and $10 kids’ tickets, and space is limited, so RSVP soon
Getting ready for a very strong El Niño: a storm-prep card on Weather, flash-flood warnings that say what to do, and City text alerts — text SCEMERGENCY to 888777
A tap-to-call “Who to call” list on the Fire page, and what to do if you find a bat — most of LA County’s rabid bats turn up in our valley
Two Fire page corrections: a nearby evacuation order no longer reads as “all clear” for our hill, and a failed earthquake check no longer counts as “nothing to report”
All six sections now fit the top of a phone screen — Weather, Living Here, Events and HOA used to be hidden behind a sideways swipe — plus bigger buttons and clearer text throughout
Fire page fixes: a shelter-in-place order now says stay inside (never “leave now”), an evacuation warning for our zone always leads, and the quiet-day summary can no longer sit on top of a real alert
Two neighborhood events are up — Burgers & Brews for the dads (Sat, Oct 3) and the 2nd Annual Halloween Party, with flyers, prices and how to RSVP
When an outside data source stops answering, the site now shows everything else instead of sitting at “unknown”
Living Here shows the next trash pickup and Burrtec’s holiday schedule, and the home page flags weeks when pickup runs a day late
Weather alerts now say when they end (“Flood Advisory until 7 PM”), and the Fire page shows every NWS alert for our location
The site notices when it’s actually raining on our hill, the home page boxes are colour-coded like the status line, and that line now says “moderate” when the air is, not “good”
Easier on a phone — bigger text and buttons everywhere, Events opens on this week’s picks, and the Fire page puts evacuation info first when it matters
New Weather page, and air quality and fire weather now come from neighbor sensors right here on our hill — not a reading from six miles away
Easier to use with a keyboard or screen reader, and the emergency status line sits where “skip to content” can’t jump past it
The COC Performing Arts Center season is in Events, plus Living Here corrections — our schools, and where paint, batteries and propane actually go
Event days are now checked against the venue’s own page — the Old Town Newhall farmers market runs Saturdays, not Sundays
Trash day is Tuesday (now on Living Here), plus a decluttering pass so quiet days show less and the important things stand out
“Smell smoke but nothing listed?” — a first-20-minutes guide on the Fire page, plus sharper warnings and easier-to-read colours
Real measured air quality from the EPA monitor in Santa Clarita, live power-outage tracking, and earthquake awareness
Neighborhood alerts — evacuation, fire and red-flag warnings auto-detected, with a one-tap WhatsApp share, plus AI-curated weekend picks every Friday
The home page leads with what’s coming up — live numbers, next events, and what’s new since your last visit
Local pros — a neighbor-shared solar & battery company on Living Here

Fires show acreage and containment from CAL FIRE with NASA satellite heat checks; Events got search and day-by-day grouping; and HOA & Resources explains your California homeowner rights in plain English
